_comment: Bare classical attributions accepted as known debt. --gate fails only on defects absent from this list. Shrink it by adding loci; never grow it to make a commit pass.
known: a craftsman who wishes to do his work well must first sharpen his tools.
a gem cannot be polished without friction, nor a man perfected without trials.
a room without books is like a body without a soul.
begin at once to live, and count each separate day as a separate life.
difficulties are things that show a person what they are.
difficulties strengthen the mind, as labor does the body.
do it now. sometimes 'later' becomes 'never.'
do not do to others what angers you if done to you by others.
do not spoil what you have by desiring what you have not.
do nothing which is of no use.
drops of water hollow out the stone, not by force but by falling often.
employ your time in improving yourself by other men's writings, so that you shall gain easily what others have labored hard for.
first say to yourself what you would be; and then do what you have to do.
fortune favors the bold.
fortune sides with him who dares.
gratitude is not only the greatest of virtues, but the parent of all the others.
happiness depends upon ourselves.
he who begins is half the work; dare to be wise: begin!
he who has begun has half done. dare to know; begin!
he who has never learned to obey cannot be a good commander.
he who is prudent and lies in wait for an enemy who is not, will be victorious.
humility is the solid foundation of all virtues.
i cannot teach anybody anything. i can only make them think.
i prefer a short life with width to a narrow one with length.
if you know the enemy and know yourself, you need not fear the result of a hundred battles.
in battle, if you make your opponent flinch, you have already won.
it is not because things are difficult that we do not dare; it is because we do not dare that things are difficult.
knowing yourself is the beginning of all wisdom.
no man ever steps in the same river twice, for it's not the same river and he's not the same man.
no man is free who is not master of himself.
perceive that which cannot be seen with the eye.
pleasure in the job puts perfection in the work.
prudence is the knowledge of things to be sought, and those to be shunned.
real knowledge is to know the extent of one's ignorance.
step by step walk the thousand-mile road.
study the past if you would define the future.
take rest; a field that has rested gives a bountiful crop.
the beginning is the most important part of the work.
the happiness of your life depends upon the quality of your thoughts.
the journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step.
the mind is not a vessel to be filled, but a fire to be kindled.
the superior man acts before he speaks, and afterwards speaks according to his action.
the superior man, when resting in safety, does not forget that danger may come.
the unexamined life is not worth living.
the wound is the place where the light enters you.
there is nothing outside of the momentary determination of a single thought.
to attain knowledge, add things every day. to attain wisdom, remove things every day.
to make no mistakes is not in the power of man; but from their errors the wise and good learn wisdom for the future.
today is victory over yourself of yesterday; tomorrow is your victory over lesser men.
very little is needed to make a happy life; it is all within yourself, in your way of thinking.
victorious warriors win first and then go to war.
waste no more time arguing about what a good man should be. be one.
wear gratitude like a cloak, and it will feed every corner of your life.
well begun is half done.
what you seek is seeking you.
when you do things from your soul, you feel a river moving in you, a joy.
while we are postponing, life speeds by.
